editors.name: OpenCode
highlights: OpenCode Terminal: Install, Agents & Alternatives | AI/TLDR
OpenCode | Press kit with company facts and brand assets

Everyone is making OpenCode videos. Most show a quick demo and stop. This one covers what it is, how to install it, how to use it, and whether it’s worth your time. 💻

OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent. It runs in your terminal, as a desktop app, or in your browser.

What’s inside:
📊 The numbers: MIT license, 75+ providers, 160K+ GitHub stars
⚙️ Install: curl, Homebrew, npm, or the desktop app
🚀 First run: /connect, then /init
🤖 Two agents: build edits files, plan is read-only
🧪 An example workflow, with /undo
🔒 Config: make it ask before any change
⚠️ The honest part: speed, cost, privacy, provider rules

Next steps:

Install it and open a small test project
Run /connect, then /init
Use plan first, then build, and read every change
Run one real task in your current tool and in OpenCode, and compare time, cost and quality

Don’t trust the hype. Test it on your own code.

Notes:

Install commands follow the official docs as of November 2026 (OpenCode 2). Older tutorials use a different command, so if one fails, check opencode.ai/docs.
The example session is illustrative, not a recording.
The 7.5M monthly users figure is reported by secondary sources and isn’t audited.

Sources: opencode.ai docs and README, developersdigest.tech, tech-insider.org, glukhov.org
